WV12-P04.4.note: A bank that sits on a named street and pulls down its shutters at closing time is a business, listed alongside the church clock and the school as the town shutting for the evening; the bird cloud is described separately and is never called a bank.

support: I laughed out loud the first evening I saw it myself: a chimney that has burned nothing for eleven years, drawing a cloud of smoke down into itself.
Until they go, every clear evening the old chimney smokes in reverse over the schoolyard, and I stand at the gate grinning up at it.
WV12-P04.5.note: Read literally, the writer laughs out loud at the chimney and grins up at it every evening, delighted by the joke of a cold chimney that seems to smoke backwards; nothing the writer says expresses esteem, disapproval, sorrow or worry.
